items.reason: Barnard's 'which may contribute to joint results' makes contribution optional, so 'exists only when it contributes' is strongly implied false, but the source never states non-contributing informal organisations exist, so the rejection of B rests on a modal inference.

The stem says 'sell one more quintal' after 'every unit', and option B refers to 'earlier ones', so output is already positive and D (Rs 40 x total output) is not MR; the one-quintal edge case is a strained reading, and the excerpt states MR is precisely the market price.

The syllabus lists 'Steps in staffing process' and the cited excerpt is the textbook's Compensation step, so it is arguably in scope, but the time-based/performance-based pay-plan detail is not named in the syllabus bullets, so the syllabus-fit rejection is defensible.

The syllabus lists the two-sector income determination and multiplier mechanism but its open-economy unit covers only BoP and exchange rates; the import-leakage effect on the multiplier is not a listed topic.

The passage says the organiser 'shortened each speaker's time' and the teacher's question drove the cuts, so 'only' merely paraphrases that, and nothing in the passage says the organiser chose the cuts; the rejection nitpicks an incidental word.

Option B itself stipulates the history is one 'that nobody asked for', so it is by construction not 'only the information that is necessary', which decisively fails the supplied definition of concise.
